1 · Starting-shape search

The search varies placement, two bending directions, twist and a rounded fold while preserving material volume and the target geometry.

2 · Geometric containment check

A proposed starting piece must lie inside native cartilage with the same 0.8 mm research margin.

3 · Forming and attachment model

Elastic equilibria are calculated under temporary guides and tension-only stitches to fixed neighboring pieces, including states after guide removal.

The 5%, 10% and 20% strain screens are exploratory settings, not established safe bending limits. This is a limited deformation model, not a validated prediction of tissue damage, suture failure or a complete assembled ear.

What holds the shape?

During forming, temporary guides can push and pull. A stitch can only pull; it goes slack when its ends move closer than its set length. The model removes the guides after the stitches are engaged.

Attachment locations are automatic engineering proposals based on nearby framework surfaces. Neighboring pieces are held fixed. Their shared deformation, contact and stitch pull-through still require a more complete model and physical testing.

What the evidence supports

    Methods, verification and downloads

    Two isochoric cylindrical bends, a globally invertible twist and a rounded-fold shear define a restricted family of shapes. Elastic energy is integrated through the volume. The method cannot yet express every branch motion or localized deformation. A sharp crease or scored hinge is not modeled.

    The target surface is preserved by subdivision before deformation; no ear resizing is used. Whole-solid native-mask certification is separate from sampled strain estimates and conditional holding forces. The force model does not include viscoelasticity, cutting-induced warping, damage, calcification or measured stitch strength.

    SummaryValidation summaryHolding-force checksResearch settingsMethods & sources
    A shape that can be cut is not automatically a shape that tissue can safely form and retain. Failed searches are retained; they are not impossibility proofs.
